title: Quick check: Systematic Troubleshooting

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Systematic Troubleshooting”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Reproducing the issue should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.
questions.answer_key: Reproducing the issue should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Systematic Troubleshooting: Reproducing the issue should verify what the learner can observe with repeatable tests, including a failure case.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Reproducing the issue?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Systematic Troubleshooting: Assert through roles, labels, and visible results rather than component internals.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Systematic Troubleshooting” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Systematic Troubleshooting: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
